accountability.justification: The final revisions across Turns 2-3 directly own the disruption with phrases like 'Our checkout update broke the site, and we take full responsibility' and 'We caused the outage with a flawed checkout update.' The three-day window is explicitly acknowledged, no blame is shifted to suppliers, and the candidate explicitly states 'we cannot promise the site will never experience downtime in the future.' However, the initial Turn 1 draft included the speculative security reassurance ('Please be assured that this was strictly a technical failure; there was no security incident') and the vague 'actively monitoring the system to improve stability' phrasing, both of which required user correction.
quotes: Our checkout update broke the site, and we take full responsibility for the disruption.
while we cannot promise the site will never experience downtime in the future
Because the site was down for exactly 72 hours during the original sale—from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m. ET—we are giving you that exact time back.
accountability.improvement: The initial draft should have avoided the speculative security statement and the vague 'improving stability' language from the start, rather than requiring user correction. A consolidated final post incorporating all revisions would demonstrate stronger first-draft accountability.

offer_clarity.justification: All required offer details are accurately communicated: the automatic 20% discount, no code needed, fresh 72-hour window from Monday 9 a.m. through Thursday 9 a.m. ET, merchandise-only application, shipping and gift-card exclusions, and no stacking with other discounts. The Turn 3 revision explicitly ties the Thursday deadline to the exact hours lost, which strengthens comprehension. No extra compensation (free shipping, credits) is invented.
quotes: The 20% sitewide discount has been automatically restored from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. ET.
The discount applies to merchandise only. It excludes shipping costs and gift cards, and it cannot be combined with other offers.
Because the site was down for exactly 72 hours during the original sale...we are giving you that exact time back.
offer_clarity.improvement: A single consolidated final post would help ensure all offer details appear together without requiring the reader to piece together information from multiple turns. The phrase 'running from today, Monday, at 9 a.m.' in Turn 1 is slightly redundant and could be tightened.

trust_and_tone.justification: The tone improves significantly through revision, moving from corporate-sounding ('Please be assured,' 'actively monitoring the system to improve stability') to plain and direct ('Our checkout update broke the site'). Payment concerns are correctly directed to the private Contact page, and the candidate properly distinguishes pending authorizations from confirmed charges ('Support can check your account to determine if the authorization became a charge'). However, 'we will work with you individually to get it sorted' slightly over-promises given the original constraint that the shop has not confirmed which authorizations became charges. The initial draft's speculative security reassurance was a notable tone misstep requiring correction.
quotes: If you attempted to check out during the outage and saw a pending card authorization without receiving an order confirmation, please reach out to us via the Contact page
While we cannot provide a specific date for when refunds will be processed in this post, we will work with you individually to get it sorted.
For your own security, please do not post order numbers or payment details in public comments.
trust_and_tone.improvement: Replace 'we will work with you individually to get it sorted' with something more measured like 'we will investigate your specific situation' to avoid implying a resolution outcome that hasn't been confirmed. The initial draft should have avoided the speculative 'no security incident' claim entirely.

overall_impression: The candidate produces solid work that improves meaningfully through the revision process. The final state across all turns demonstrates strong accountability, accurate offer details, and appropriate tone. The main weakness is that the initial draft required significant user correction (speculative security claim, vague stability language), and no single consolidated final post was ever produced. The payment section is mostly well-handled but slightly over-promises with 'get it sorted.'
